questions.question: What is the speed of sound in air?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**343 m/sec**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The speed of sound in air is approximately **343 meters per second (m/sec)** at standard temperature and pressure conditions.
 
• This speed can vary depending on factors such as temperature, humidity, and altitude.
 
• At higher temperatures, the speed of sound increases because the molecules in the air move faster.
 
• Similarly, higher humidity levels can slightly increase the speed of sound, as moist air is less dense than dry air.
 
• In general, the speed of sound in air is a crucial parameter in various fields, including acoustics, aeronautics, and meteorology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The speed of sound in other mediums is different; for example, it is much higher in water (approximately 1482 m/sec) and even higher in solids.
 
• The speed of sound is an essential factor in the design and analysis of various systems, including sonar, ultrasound imaging, and audio equipment.
 
• Understanding the speed of sound is also crucial for studying phenomena such as sonic booms and the Doppler effect.

questions.question:
When a wave goes from one medium to another, there is a change in-

I. Velocity

II. Amplitude

III. Frequency

IV. Wavelength

Choose the correct option-
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Sound: A sound is a form of energy that produces the sensation of hearing in our ears.
 
• **Wave **is the propagation of disturbance from one place to another in an organized manner.
 
• Waves can be mechanical waves or non-mechanical waves.
 
• Mechanical waves like sound waves, require a medium to propagate.
 
• The** wavelength** is defined as the distance between the crests or troughs of a wave motion. 

Amplitude:

 
• Amplitude is the measure of compression or rarefaction of particles of a medium through which sound is traveling.
 
• The higher the amplitude, the louder the sound.
 
• The amplitude A is related to loudness as loudness ∝ A2

Frequency:

 
• Frequency refers to the rate of vibration of sound.
 
• The pitch of a sound is decided by the measure of frequency.
 
• The higher the frequency, the shriller the sound.
 
• Frequency measured in Hertz (Hz).

**Explanation:**__

 
• The basic properties of a wave are wavelength, frequency, time period, speed, and amplitude.
 
• When a sound wave goes from one medium to another, the **wavelength changes** but **the frequency remains unchanged **because the frequency of sound depends upon the source of the sound.
 
• The relation between wavelength, frequency, and speed is,
 
 
• **v = f × λ **
 
 
 
• The velocity of sound depends upon the elasticity and inertia of the medium. Hence, **velocity changes** when a wave goes from one medium to another.
 
• When a particle moves from one medium to another, its **amplitude increases **on decreases depending upon the medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3cdad83bb84503735cb0fc63a9728ac9243a695a27abf471aac997e10a1ad51.png] 

Thus, **the correct answer is I, II, and IV. **

questions.question: The velocity of sound in air
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Option 3.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• In physics, **sound **is a vibration that propagates as an acoustic wave, through a transmission medium such as a gas, liquid or solid. 
 
• Sound can propagate through a medium such as air, water and solids as longitudinal waves and also as a transverse wave in solids.
 
• The behaviour of sound propagation is generally affected by the following things:
 
 
• A complex relationship between the density and pressure of the medium. This relationship, affected by temperature, determines the speed of sound within the medium. 
 
 
• The velocity of sound **increases with an increase in temperature. **Hence, Option 3 is the correct answer.
 
 
 
• The velocity of sound in air **increases with an increase in humidity**.** **
 
• The velocity of sound in air is **independent of amplitude and frequency.**
 
• The velocity of sound in air is independent of pressure.
 
• The motion of the medium itself: If the medium is moving, this movement may increase or decrease the absolute speed of the sound wave depending on the direction of the movement.
 
 
• **For example**, sound moving through wind will have its speed of propagation increased by the speed of the wind if the sound and wind are moving in the same direction. If the sound and wind are moving in opposite directions, the speed of the sound wave will be decreased by the speed of the wind.
 
 
 
• The viscosity of the medium. Medium viscosity determines the rate at which sound is attenuated. For many media, such as air or water, attenuation due to viscosity is negligible.

questions.question: A person burned a firecracker in front of a cliff and heard its echo 5 s after it burst. The distance of the cliff from the person, if the speed of the sound is 340 m/s, is close to
questions.solution:
__**Concept**__:

__
 
• To calculate the distance of the cliff from the person, we need to consider the time it took for the sound to travel from the person to the cliff and back as an echo.
 
• The sound traveled from the person to the cliff, and then the echo traveled back to the person.
 
• So the total time it took for the sound to travel is twice the time it took to hear the echo.

**Calculation:**__

Given that

The echo was heard 5 seconds after the firecracker burst, we can determine the time it took for the sound to travel from the person to the cliff and back as 5 seconds divided by 2, which is 2.5 seconds.

T = 2.5 sec

Using the formula:

Distance = Speed × Time, we can calculate the distance of the cliff from the person:

Distance = 340 m/s × 2.5 s = 850 meters

Therefore, the distance of the cliff from the person is approximately 850 meters.

**The correct answer is option (4)**

questions.question: When you increase the loudness of the ringtone of your mobile phone, the frequency of ringtone
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**remains same**__.

__**Concept:**__

**Sound**

__
 
• Sound is a form of energy which produces a sensation of hearing in our ears.
 
• Sound is produced by vibrating objects. The matter or substance through which sound is transmitted is called a medium. It can be solid, liquid or gas. 

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• As the **loudness of the mobile ringtone increases**__, the __**frequency of the ringtone remains same.**__
 
• The loudness is expressed in a unit called **decibel **(dB). 
 
• Loudness is the physical response of the ear to the intensity of sound.
 
• A sound with more energy is referred to as a **strong sound.**
 
• Loudness of sound is **proportional to the square of the amplitude **of the vibration producing the sound. 
 
• **Loudness ∝ (amplitude)²**
 
• The** loudness of sound waves does not depend on the frequency** of the sound waves. 
 
• **Loudness and Amplitude: **Loudness is the perception of how intense or strong a sound seems to our ears. It is directly related to the amplitude of a sound wave.
 __
 
• Increasing the amplitude increases the loudness, while decreasing the amplitude decreases the loudness.
 
 
 
• **Frequency and Pitch:** Frequency is the number of oscillations (cycles) that a sound wave completes in one second, measured in Hertz (Hz).
 
 
• Pitch is the perceptual attribute of the sound that allows us to classify it as higher or lower; it is directly related to the frequency of the sound wave.
 
• Higher frequency corresponds to a higher pitch, and lower frequency corresponds to a lower pitch.
 
 
 
• **Intensity and Energy: **Intensity is the amount of energy a sound wave carries per unit area per unit time, and it is proportional to the square of the amplitude.

Higher intensity results in louder sounds but does not affect the frequency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

__
 
• Loudness is related to amplitude.
 
• Pitch is related to frequency.
 
• Intensity is associated with energy of the sound wave and is proportional to amplitude squared.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When the **amplitude is greater,** the l**oudness of the sound is also higher. **
 
• When the **amplitude is low,** the **sound produced will be dim.**

questions.solution:

**Concept-**

__
 
• Any unwanted sound that causes annoyance, burning and pain in the human ear is called noise.
 
• Noise is measured in dB units which indicates the loudness of the sound.
 
• Noise level refers to the decibel level of noise produced by any equipment or machine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__
 
• The strength of the noise is called the decibel unit (dB), we can measure the level of noise with a sound level meter.
 
• A logarithmic scale is used to describe sound levels meaningfully in digits that are better manageable, using 10 as the base, rather than a linear one.
 
• This scale is called the decibel scale. A whisper is about 30 dB, regular talk is about 60 dB, and it's about 95 dB to run a motorcycle engine.
 
• Noise in excess of 70 dB can damage hearing over a long period of time.
 
• Loud sounds above 120 dB will cause immediate damage to the ears. So, sound exceeding 80 dB is harmful to the human ear.

**The complication of excessive noise-**

 
• Excessive noise pollution affects millions of people every day. The most common health problem it causes is noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL). Exposure to loud noises can also lead to high blood pressure, heart disease, sleep disturbances and stress. These health problems can affect all age groups, especially children.
 
• Hearing loss in adults includes:
 
 
• excessive noise
 
• inheritance
 
• head injury
 
• infection
 
• disease
 
• certain prescription drugs
 
• circulatory problems such as high blood pressure
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The acceptable noise level in India has been determined by the CPCB for different areas. The allowable maximum in industrial areas is 75 dB during the day and 70 dB at night. In commercial areas, it is 65 dB and 55 dB, while in residential neighbourhoods it is 55 dB and 45 dB during the day and night respectively. Also, there is a category called 'silent zone' which comes within 100 meters of the premises of schools, colleges, hospitals, and courts. In this region, the allowable noise limit is 5.
 
• The three basic categories of hearing loss are sensorineural hearing loss, conductive hearing loss, and mixed hearing loss.​

questions.question: Which is the incorrect statement with regard to ultrasound waves?

options.text: Ultrasound cannot be reflected back from defective locations
They travel among well-defined paths even in the presence of obstacles
They are used in industries and for medical purposes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ultrasound cannot be reflected back from defective locations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ultrasound waves are indeed high-frequency waves, typically above** 20,000 Hz**, which is higher than the upper audible limit of human hearing.
 
• Ultrasound waves have the ability to travel along well-defined paths even when obstacles are present, which makes them useful in various applications.
 
• Ultrasound waves are widely used in medical imaging (like sonography) and industrial applications (like non-destructive testing) to detect defects or for imaging purposes.
 
• Contrary to Option 1, ultrasound waves can be reflected back from defective locations; this property is used in medical diagnostics and industrial flaw detection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ultrasound Waves**

 
 
• Ultrasound waves are sound waves with frequencies higher than the **audible range for humans (greater than 20 kHz)**.
 
• They are used in various fields such as medical imaging (ultrasound scans), industrial non-destructive testing, and even in cleaning processes.
 
• In medical imaging, ultrasound waves are used to create images of the internal organs and tissues. This is done by sending high-frequency sound waves into the body and measuring the echoes that bounce back.
 
• In industry, ultrasound waves are used for detecting flaws in materials, measuring thickness, and cleaning delicate components.
 
 
 
• **Reflection of Ultrasound Waves**
 
 
• The principle of reflection of ultrasound waves is used in various applications like medical ultrasonography and industrial flaw detection.
 
• When ultrasound waves encounter a boundary between two different materials, some of the waves are reflected back to the source. The time taken for the waves to return is used to determine the distance and the nature of the boundary.
 
• This property is particularly useful in identifying and locating defects within materials, such as cracks or voids.
 
 
 
• **Path of Ultrasound Waves**
 
 
• Ultrasound waves travel in well-defined paths, and their direction can be controlled using specialized equipment.
 
• This property is exploited in ultrasound imaging, where the waves are directed to specific parts of the body to create detailed images.
 
• In industrial applications, this allows for precise inspection of materials and components.

questions.question: _________ is the persistence of sound in a particular space after the original sound is removed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reverberation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Reverberation, or reverb, is defined as** the persistence of sound in a particular space after the original sound is removed**.
 
• This process happens when a sound or signal produced in an enclosed space causes a large number of echoes to build up and then slowly decay as the sound is absorbed by the walls and air of the space.
 
• It's a **key attribute in acoustics and audio engineering **with various specific applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Streaming:** In the context of media,** streaming is a method for delivering and obtaining data**, such as audio and video, in a continuous manner from a particular source.
 
• **Radiation:** In physics,** radiation is the emission or transmission of energy in the form of waves or particles**. In an acoustic context, it refers to the distribution of sound wave energy away from a source of sound.
 
• **Vibration: **It is an **oscillation of the parts of a fluid or an elastic solid** whose equilibrium has been disturbed.
 
• While these concepts can factor into sound production or perception, they do not describe the persistence of sound in an area after the original sound is removed.

__
 
• Sound cannot travel through a **vacuum** because there are no particles to transmit the vibrations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In **gases**, sound travels the slowest because the particles are far apart.
 
• The speed of sound in air at room temperature is approximately 343 meters per second (m/s).
 
• In space, which is a near-perfect vacuum, astronauts use radios to communicate because sound cannot travel through the vacuum.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a sound wave?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electromagnetic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Electromagnetic** waves are not a characteristic of a sound wave.
 
• Electromagnetic waves differ from mechanical waves in that they do not require a medium to propagate.
 
• This means that electromagnetic waves can travel not only through the air and sol

questions.question: If the amplitude of vibration is increased to three times of its initial value, then the loudness of sound will:

options.text: be six times of its original value
become three times of its original value
become nine times of its original value

questions.solution:
__**EXPLANATION:**__

The loudness of sound depends on its amplitude.

Loudness is proportional to the square of its amplitude.

So,** loudness ∝ (amplitude)²**

Here amplitude of sound is tripled,

loudness ∝ (3 x amplitude)²

loudness ∝ (3)² x (amplitude)²

loudness ∝ 9 × (amplitude)²

**Hence, if the amplitude of a sound is tripled, loudness increases nine times.**

questions.question: What is the relation between the frequency f, wavelength λ, and speed v of the sound?
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

Sound: It is a form of energy produced by vibration or disturbance that propagates in a medium.

__
 
• It travels in the form of longitudinal waves (Compression or rarefaction)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b82b5e660f7984a80ca8aa17e891e0e40ffd516b2e8892cb4b96bc17c35bc05.png] 

 
• **Wavelength (λ)**: The distance between two successive crests or the distance between two successive troughs is called wavelength of the wave.
 
• **Frequency (f)**: The number of vibrations per second is called the frequency of the wave.
 
• Speed of sound or for that matter any wave is the product of the frequency and wavelength of that wave (since speed is the ratio of distance and time).

The correct relation between the frequency f, wavelength λ, and speed v of the sound is given by:

 v** =** f** λ**

**EXPLANATION__:**

According to the above discussion, 

v = f λ 

⇒ f = v/λ 

Hence option 1 is correct.

__**EXTRA POINTS**__:

 
• The **speed of sound** varies in different mediums of its propagation. The **speed of sound is minimum in the air **which is approx. 346** m/s**.
 
• Its speed is **greater in liquids** (approx. 1498 m/s in water) and the **greatest in solids** (approx. 5,950 m/s in iron)
